title: Complete row-unique table
observed_result: 188,318 rows, 132 columns, 188,318 unique ids, 0 duplicate rows, 0 missing cells, and 0 non-positive loss values.
interpretation: The labeled file does not need row repairs before exploratory analysis. Support, distributions, and target relationships still have to be studied.
limitation: A clean table does not show that every categorical level has enough claims to interpret, and it does not provide a future-period file.
october_implication: Keep the full table as the October source. Fit baselines only on training rows.

title: Long right tail of loss
observed_result: Mean loss is 3,037.34, median loss is 2,115.57, the 95th percentile is 8,508.54, the maximum is 121,012.25, and skewness is 3.795. 1,884 rows sit above the 99th percentile of 13,981.20.
interpretation: Most claims are near the median. A smaller set of large claims pulls the mean above the median. Those large claims stay in the severity distribution.
limitation: Nothing in this file shows that the maximum is an invalid entry. A log1p plot does not replace statistics in original loss units.
october_implication: Keep October error in original loss units. Do not drop high-loss rows in order to improve a score.

title: Mixed categorical cardinality
observed_result: All 116 categorical fields are inventoried. 72 fields have 2 levels and 88 have at most 4. cat116 has 326 levels, cat110 has 131, and cat109 has 84. 227 levels have fewer than 10 claims, and those levels appear on 616 rows. 64 levels each cover at least 90 percent of claims.
interpretation: The file mixes many low-cardinality fields with a few high-cardinality fields. Rare levels are a support issue. They are not a reason to delete rows during exploratory analysis.
limitation: Level codes are anonymous, so a difference in median loss is not a named business cause.
october_implication: October encoding has to handle rare levels and levels that appear only in later data, without learning those rules from validation rows.

title: Weak linear association with loss
observed_result: The strongest absolute Pearson correlations with raw loss are cont2 at 0.142, cont7 at 0.120, and cont3 at 0.111. Spearman correlations with loss are weaker for those same fields.
interpretation: No continuous field has a strong straight-line relationship with raw loss. That result does not measure how useful the field is inside a later model.
limitation: Pearson and Spearman describe one field at a time. They do not test interactions or a trained model.
october_implication: Do not drop a continuous field before held-out MAE testing only because its correlation with loss is small.

title: Binned loss is not flat
observed_result: Each continuous field was split with a 10-bin qcut and duplicates dropped. cont2 produced 9 bins and cont5 produced 8. cont2 mean loss moves from about 2,120 in the lowest bin to about 3,481 in the highest, while its median moves from about 1,740 to about 2,123. cont14 median loss is about 2,477 in the lowest bin and about 2,122 in the highest.
interpretation: Quantile bins show loss patterns that one correlation coefficient hides. The shape is not the same for every field.
limitation: Bin edges depend on this file. Anonymous field names do not say why a bin mean is higher.
october_implication: Compare binned and linear summaries during October validation. A bin chart is not a model score.

title: Redundant continuous predictors
observed_result: Pearson correlations are 0.994 for cont11 and cont12, 0.930 for cont1 and cont9, and 0.883 for cont6 and cont10.
interpretation: Those pairs move together. In a later linear model their separate coefficients would be hard to tell apart.
limitation: Correlation is not a decision to remove a field. The two fields may still differ on claims that matter for MAE.
october_implication: Keep both members of each pair until held-out MAE shows whether dropping one changes error.

title: Anonymous fields and one labeled file
observed_result: cat1 through cat116 and cont1 through cont14 have no stated business meaning in the source. The project has this one labeled claims file and no separate future-period file.
interpretation: September can describe this file. It cannot name a cause for a level, and it cannot show that the same patterns will hold on later claims.
limitation: A story about what an unnamed field represents would go beyond the labels in the file.
october_implication: October recommendations stay experiments tied to these tables. They are not a production reserve or a chosen model.
